🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-DYNAMIC-CLASS vendor/phpdocumentor/type-resolver/src/TypeResolver.php — Line 654 Learn more ↗
PHP dynamic class instantiation from user-controlled variable
Instantiating a PHP class from a user-supplied string (new $$userInput(), new $classFromRequest()) allows an attacker to instantiate any autoloaded class. If constructors or magic methods perform file operations, network calls, or code evaluation, this leads to remote code execution. CISA identifies this as insufficient input validation enabling injection.
new $className(
Fix: Never instantiate classes from user-supplied strings. Use an explicit allowlist: $allowed = ['Foo', 'Bar']; if (in_array($className, $allowed, true)) { $obj = new $className(); } A factory function with a match/switch on known class names is the safest pattern.
Category: CISA: Injection
🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-REMOTE-INCLUDE vendor/brianium/paratest/bin/phpunit-wrapper.php — Line 29 Learn more ↗
PHP remote or user-controlled file inclusion
When allow_url_include = On in php.ini, passing a URL to include() / require() fetches and executes arbitrary remote PHP code. Even with allow_url_include = Off, passing user input to include/require enables Local File Inclusion (LFI) and path traversal to sensitive files such as /etc/passwd or application config files. CISA identifies remote code execution via file inclusion as a critical preventable vulnerability.
require_once $file
Fix: Never pass user input to include/require. Use an allowlist of permitted files: $allowed = ['home', 'about', 'contact']; if (in_array($page, $allowed, true)) { include __DIR__ . '/pages/' . $page . '.php'; } Also set allow_url_include = Off in php.ini.
Category: CISA: Injection

🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-TYPE-JUGGLING vendor/sebastian/lines-of-code/src/LinesOfCode.php — Line 47 Learn more ↗
PHP loose equality (==) used with password, hash, or token value
PHP's loose equality operator (==) performs type coercion before comparing. This enables 'magic hash' exploits where hash strings beginning with '0e' are coerced to 0.0 in scientific notation and compare equal to any other '0e...' hash string. Comparing a numeric-looking user string with == 0 evaluates to true in PHP < 8. CISA identifies weak authentication logic as a preventable root cause of authentication failures.
== $nonCommentLinesOfCode
Fix: Use strict equality (===) for all security-sensitive comparisons in PHP. For password verification use password_verify(), which performs a constant-time comparison. For HMAC or token comparison use hash_equals($known, $provided).
Category: CISA: Authentication Failures

🔴 CRITICAL PHP-IV-FILE-UPLOAD-EXTENSION vendor/guzzlehttp/psr7/src/UploadedFile.php — Line 149 Learn more ↗
Uploaded file stored without extension allowlist check
Storing uploaded files without validating the file extension against an allowlist allows attackers to upload .php, .phtml, .phar, .asp, and other executable files that can be triggered to execute server-side code.
move_uploaded_file($this->file, $targetPath)
Fix: Validate the extension: $ext = strtolower(pathinfo($name, PATHINFO_EXTENSION)); $allowed = ['jpg','jpeg','png','gif','pdf']; if (!in_array($ext, $allowed, true)) { die('File type not permitted'); } Also verify the MIME type with finfo_file().
Category: Input Validation
🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-UNSERIALIZE vendor/phpunit/phpunit/src/TextUI/Configuration/SourceMapper.php — Line 51 Learn more ↗
PHP unserialize() called with user-controlled data
Passing user-supplied data to PHP's unserialize() allows Object Injection attacks. If the codebase contains gadget chains (magic methods such as __wakeup(), __destruct(), or __toString()), an attacker can trigger arbitrary code execution, file deletion, or other destructive actions. CISA lists insecure deserialization as a root cause of preventable vulnerabilities.
unserialize($content
Fix: Never deserialize data from untrusted sources. Use json_decode() for data interchange. If PHP objects must be transferred, use a signed token format (e.g. JWT) and validate the signature before deserializing. Alternatively, use the Symfony Serializer with an explicit type allowlist.
Category: CISA: Insecure Deserialization

If constructors or magic methods perform file operations, network calls, or code evaluation, this leads to remote code execution. CISA identifies this as insufficient input validation enabling injection.
new $className(
Fix: Never instantiate classes from user-supplied strings. Use an explicit allowlist: $allowed = ['Foo', 'Bar']; if (in_array($className, $allowed, true)) { $obj = new $className(); } A factory function with a match/switch on known class names is the safest pattern.
Category: CISA: Injection

Use of eval() or Function() with dynamic input
eval() and new Function() execute arbitrary code. Passing user data to them is a critical code-injection risk.

Fix: Avoid eval(). Use safer alternatives such as JSON.parse() for data or a well-tested expression parser.

🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-UNSERIALIZE vendor/ramsey/uuid/src/Provider/Node/NodeProviderCollection.php — Line 43 Learn more ↗
PHP unserialize() called with user-controlled data
Passing user-supplied data to PHP's unserialize() allows Object Injection attacks. If the codebase contains gadget chains (magic methods such as __wakeup(), __destruct(), or __toString()), an attacker can trigger arbitrary code execution, file deletion, or other destructive actions. CISA lists insecure deserialization as a root cause of preventable vulnerabilities.
unserialize($serialized
Fix: Never deserialize data from untrusted sources. Use json_decode() for data interchange. If PHP objects must be transferred, use a signed token format (e.g. JWT) and validate the signature before deserializing. Alternatively, use the Symfony Serializer with an explicit type allowlist.
Category: CISA: Insecure Deserialization

🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-REMOTE-INCLUDE vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/View/Compilers/BladeCompiler.php — Line 944 Learn more ↗
PHP remote or user-controlled file inclusion
When allow_url_include = On in php.ini, passing a URL to include() / require() fetches and executes arbitrary remote PHP code. Even with allow_url_include = Off, passing user input to include/require enables Local File Inclusion (LFI) and path traversal to sensitive files such as /etc/passwd or application config files. CISA identifies remote code execution via file inclusion as a critical preventable vulnerability.
include($path
Fix: Never pass user input to include/require. Use an allowlist of permitted files: $allowed = ['home', 'about', 'contact']; if (in_array($page, $allowed, true)) { include __DIR__ . '/pages/' . $page . '.php'; } Also set allow_url_include = Off in php.ini.
Category: CISA: Injection

🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-TYPE-JUGGLING vendor/symfony/routing/RouteCompiler.php — Line 249 Learn more ↗
PHP loose equality (==) used with password, hash, or token value
PHP's loose equality operator (==) performs type coercion before comparing. This enables 'magic hash' exploits where hash strings beginning with '0e' are coerced to 0.0 in scientific notation and compare equal to any other '0e...' hash string. Comparing a numeric-looking user string with == 0 evaluates to true in PHP < 8. CISA identifies weak authentication logic as a preventable root cause of authentication failures.
== $tokens
Fix: Use strict equality (===) for all security-sensitive comparisons in PHP. For password verification use password_verify(), which performs a constant-time comparison. For HMAC or token comparison use hash_equals($known, $provided).
Category: CISA: Authentication Failures

🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-UNSERIALIZE vendor/psy/psysh/src/ExecutionLoop/ProcessForker.php — Line 163 Learn more ↗
PHP unserialize() called with user-controlled data
Passing user-supplied data to PHP's unserialize() allows Object Injection attacks. If the codebase contains gadget chains (magic methods such as __wakeup(), __destruct(), or __toString()), an attacker can trigger arbitrary code execution, file deletion, or other destructive actions. CISA lists insecure deserialization as a root cause of preventable vulnerabilities.
unserialize($content
Fix: Never deserialize data from untrusted sources. Use json_decode() for data interchange. If PHP objects must be transferred, use a signed token format (e.g. JWT) and validate the signature before deserializing. Alternatively, use the Symfony Serializer with an explicit type allowlist.
Category: CISA: Insecure Deserialization

PHP's loose equality operator (==) performs type coercion before comparing. This enables 'magic hash' exploits where hash strings beginning with '0e' are coerced to 0.0 in scientific notation and compare equal to any other '0e...' hash string. Comparing a numeric-looking user string with == 0 evaluates to true in PHP < 8. CISA identifies weak authentication logic as a preventable root cause of authentication failures.
== $exitCode
Fix: Use strict equality (===) for all security-sensitive comparisons in PHP. For password verification use password_verify(), which performs a constant-time comparison. For HMAC or token comparison use hash_equals($known, $provided).
Category: CISA: Authentication Failures
🔴 CRITICAL A03-EVAL-INJECTION vendor/nikic/php-parser/lib/PhpParser/Node/Expr/Eval_.php — Line 12 Learn more ↗
Use of eval() or Function() with dynamic input
eval() and new Function() execute arbitrary code. Passing user data to them is a critical code-injection risk.
eval(
Fix: Avoid eval(). Use safer alternatives such as JSON.parse() for data or a well-tested expression parser.
Category: A03: Injection
🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-UNSERIALIZE vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Bus/DynamoBatchRepository.php — Line 514 Learn more ↗
PHP unserialize() called with user-controlled data
Passing user-supplied data to PHP's unserialize() allows Object Injection attacks. If the codebase contains gadget chains (magic methods such as __wakeup(), __destruct(), or __toString()), an attacker can trigger arbitrary code execution, file deletion, or other destructive actions. CISA lists insecure deserialization as a root cause of preventable vulnerabilities.
unserialize($serialized
Fix: Never deserialize data from untrusted sources. Use json_decode() for data interchange. If PHP objects must be transferred, use a signed token format (e.g. JWT) and validate the signature before deserializing. Alternatively, use the Symfony Serializer with an explicit type allowlist.
Category: CISA: Insecure Deserialization

🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-DYNAMIC-CLASS vendor/nikic/php-parser/lib/PhpParser/JsonDecoder.php — Line 78 Learn more ↗
PHP dynamic class instantiation from user-controlled variable
Instantiating a PHP class from a user-supplied string (new $$userInput(), new $classFromRequest()) allows an attacker to instantiate any autoloaded class. If constructors or magic methods perform file operations, network calls, or code evaluation, this leads to remote code execution. CISA identifies this as insufficient input validation enabling injection.
new $className(
Fix: Never instantiate classes from user-supplied strings. Use an explicit allowlist: $allowed = ['Foo', 'Bar']; if (in_array($className, $allowed, true)) { $obj = new $className(); } A factory function with a match/switch on known class names is the safest pattern.
Category: CISA: Injection

🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-REMOTE-INCLUDE vendor/nesbot/carbon/src/Carbon/AbstractTranslator.php — Line 423 Learn more ↗
PHP remote or user-controlled file inclusion
When allow_url_include = On in php.ini, passing a URL to include() / require() fetches and executes arbitrary remote PHP code. Even with allow_url_include = Off, passing user input to include/require enables Local File Inclusion (LFI) and path traversal to sensitive files such as /etc/passwd or application config files. CISA identifies remote code execution via file inclusion as a critical preventable vulnerability.
include $file
Fix: Never pass user input to include/require. Use an allowlist of permitted files: $allowed = ['home', 'about', 'contact']; if (in_array($page, $allowed, true)) { include __DIR__ . '/pages/' . $page . '.php'; } Also set allow_url_include = Off in php.ini.
Category: CISA: Injection

🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-DYNAMIC-CLASS vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Database/Query/JoinClause.php — Line 143 Learn more ↗
PHP dynamic class instantiation from user-controlled variable
Instantiating a PHP class from a user-supplied string (new $$userInput(), new $classFromRequest()) allows an attacker to instantiate any autoloaded class. If constructors or magic methods perform file operations, network calls, or code evaluation, this leads to remote code execution. CISA identifies this as insufficient input validation enabling injection.
new $class(
Fix: Never instantiate classes from user-supplied strings. Use an explicit allowlist: $allowed = ['Foo', 'Bar']; if (in_array($className, $allowed, true)) { $obj = new $className(); } A factory function with a match/switch on known class names is the safest pattern.
Category: CISA: Injection

eval() and new Function() execute arbitrary code. Passing user data to them is a critical code-injection risk.
eval(
Fix: Avoid eval(). Use safer alternatives such as JSON.parse() for data or a well-tested expression parser.

🔴 CRITICAL PHP-IV-FILE-UPLOAD-EXTENSION vendor/symfony/http-foundation/File/UploadedFile.php — Line 192 Learn more ↗
Uploaded file stored without extension allowlist check
Storing uploaded files without validating the file extension against an allowlist allows attackers to upload .php, .phtml, .phar, .asp, and other executable files that can be triggered to execute server-side code.
move_uploaded_file($this->getPathname()
Fix: Validate the extension: $ext = strtolower(pathinfo($name, PATHINFO_EXTENSION)); $allowed = ['jpg','jpeg','png','gif','pdf']; if (!in_array($ext, $allowed, true)) { die('File type not permitted'); } Also verify the MIME type with finfo_file().
Category: Input Validation

Hardcoded secret or password
Secrets, API keys, and passwords must not be hardcoded in source code. They can be extracted from the repository.
password='.$connection['

Category: A02: Cryptographic Failures
🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-UNSERIALIZE vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Cache/ArrayStore.php — Line 72 Learn more ↗
PHP unserialize() called with user-controlled data
Passing user-supplied data to PHP's unserialize() allows Object Injection attacks. If the codebase contains gadget chains (magic methods such as __wakeup(), __destruct(), or __toString()), an attacker can trigger arbitrary code execution, file deletion, or other destructive actions. CISA lists insecure deserialization as a root cause of preventable vulnerabilities.
unserialize($data
Fix: Never deserialize data from untrusted sources. Use json_decode() for data interchange. If PHP objects must be transferred, use a signed token format (e.g. JWT) and validate the signature before deserializing. Alternatively, use the Symfony Serializer with an explicit type allowlist.
Category: CISA: Insecure Deserialization

🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-TYPE-JUGGLING vendor/symfony/event-dispatcher/Debug/TraceableEventDispatcher.php — Line 156 Learn more ↗
PHP loose equality (==) used with password, hash, or token value
PHP's loose equality operator (==) performs type coercion before comparing. This enables 'magic hash' exploits where hash strings beginning with '0e' are coerced to 0.0 in scientific notation and compare equal to any other '0e...' hash string. Comparing a numeric-looking user string with == 0 evaluates to true in PHP < 8. CISA identifies weak authentication logic as a preventable root cause of authentication failures.
== $hash
Fix: Use strict equality (===) for all security-sensitive comparisons in PHP. For password verification use password_verify(), which performs a constant-time comparison. For HMAC or token comparison use hash_equals($known, $provided).
Category: CISA: Authentication Failures

🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-REMOTE-INCLUDE vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Foundation/Bootstrap/LoadConfiguration.php — Line 115 Learn more ↗
PHP remote or user-controlled file inclusion
When allow_url_include = On in php.ini, passing a URL to include() / require() fetches and executes arbitrary remote PHP code. Even with allow_url_include = Off, passing user input to include/require enables Local File Inclusion (LFI) and path traversal to sensitive files such as /etc/passwd or application config files. CISA identifies remote code execution via file inclusion as a critical preventable vulnerability.
require $path
Fix: Never pass user input to include/require. Use an allowlist of permitted files: $allowed = ['home', 'about', 'contact']; if (in_array($page, $allowed, true)) { include __DIR__ . '/pages/' . $page . '.php'; } Also set allow_url_include = Off in php.ini.
Category: CISA: Injection

A PHP variable is interpolated or concatenated into a SQL string. If this variable holds any user-controlled value (even indirectly), the query is vulnerable to injection. Verify the variable is never user-controlled, or switch to prepared statements.

🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-REMOTE-INCLUDE vendor/voku/portable-ascii/src/voku/helper/ASCII.php — Line 1612 Learn more ↗
PHP remote or user-controlled file inclusion
When allow_url_include = On in php.ini, passing a URL to include() / require() fetches and executes arbitrary remote PHP code. Even with allow_url_include = Off, passing user input to include/require enables Local File Inclusion (LFI) and path traversal to sensitive files such as /etc/passwd or application config files. CISA identifies remote code execution via file inclusion as a critical preventable vulnerability.
include $file
Fix: Never pass user input to include/require. Use an allowlist of permitted files: $allowed = ['home', 'about', 'contact']; if (in_array($page, $allowed, true)) { include __DIR__ . '/pages/' . $page . '.php'; } Also set allow_url_include = Off in php.ini.
Category: CISA: Injection

vendor/symfony/polyfill-ctype/Ctype.php 11 warning
🟡 WARNING PHP-IV-REGEX-NO-ANCHORS vendor/symfony/polyfill-ctype/Ctype.php — Line 36 Learn more ↗
preg_match() pattern missing start/end anchors
A regex used for validation without ^ and $ anchors only checks for a match anywhere in the string. An attacker can prepend or append malicious content that still satisfies the regex. OWASP recommends anchoring all validation patterns.
preg_match('/[^A-Za-z0-9]/'
Fix: Anchor validation patterns: preg_match('/^[a-z0-9]{1,32}$/i', $input). The ^ asserts start-of-string and $ asserts end-of-string.
Category: Input Validation

🟡 WARNING PHP-SQL-VARIABLE vendor/symfony/http-foundation/Session/Storage/Handler/PdoSessionHandler.php — Line 392 Learn more ↗
Potential SQL injection via PHP variable in query
A PHP variable is interpolated or concatenated into a SQL string. If this variable holds any user-controlled value (even indirectly), the query is vulnerable to injection. Verify the variable is never user-controlled, or switch to prepared statements.
$sql = "DELETE FROM $this->table WHERE $this
Fix: Use PDO or MySQLi prepared statements with bound parameters. If this variable is intentionally hardcoded and never user-controlled, add an owasp-ignore comment above the line with a brief justification.

vendor/symfony/error-handler/DebugClassLoader.php 5 critical6 warning
🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-REMOTE-INCLUDE vendor/symfony/error-handler/DebugClassLoader.php — Line 319 Learn more ↗
PHP remote or user-controlled file inclusion
When allow_url_include = On in php.ini, passing a URL to include() / require() fetches and executes arbitrary remote PHP code. Even with allow_url_include = Off, passing user input to include/require enables Local File Inclusion (LFI) and path traversal to sensitive files such as /etc/passwd or application config files. CISA identifies remote code execution via file inclusion as a critical preventable vulnerability.
include $file
Fix: Never pass user input to include/require. Use an allowlist of permitted files: $allowed = ['home', 'about', 'contact']; if (in_array($page, $allowed, true)) { include __DIR__ . '/pages/' . $page . '.php'; } Also set allow_url_include = Off in php.ini.
Category: CISA: Injection

🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-TYPE-JUGGLING vendor/symfony/error-handler/DebugClassLoader.php — Line 1227 Learn more ↗
PHP loose equality (==) used with password, hash, or token value
PHP's loose equality operator (==) performs type coercion before comparing. This enables 'magic hash' exploits where hash strings beginning with '0e' are coerced to 0.0 in scientific notation and compare equal to any other '0e...' hash string. Comparing a numeric-looking user string with == 0 evaluates to true in PHP < 8. CISA identifies weak authentication logic as a preventable root cause of authentication failures.
== $code
Fix: Use strict equality (===) for all security-sensitive comparisons in PHP. For password verification use password_verify(), which performs a constant-time comparison. For HMAC or token comparison use hash_equals($known, $provided).
Category: CISA: Authentication Failures

🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-TYPE-JUGGLING vendor/symfony/routing/RouteCompiler.php — Line 249 Learn more ↗
PHP loose equality (==) used with password, hash, or token value
PHP's loose equality operator (==) performs type coercion before comparing. This enables 'magic hash' exploits where hash strings beginning with '0e' are coerced to 0.0 in scientific notation and compare equal to any other '0e...' hash string. Comparing a numeric-looking user string with == 0 evaluates to true in PHP < 8. CISA identifies weak authentication logic as a preventable root cause of authentication failures.
== $tokens
Fix: Use strict equality (===) for all security-sensitive comparisons in PHP. For password verification use password_verify(), which performs a constant-time comparison. For HMAC or token comparison use hash_equals($known, $provided).
Category: CISA: Authentication Failures

PHP remote or user-controlled file inclusion
When allow_url_include = On in php.ini, passing a URL to include() / require() fetches and executes arbitrary remote PHP code. Even with allow_url_include = Off, passing user input to include/require enables Local File Inclusion (LFI) and path traversal to sensitive files such as /etc/passwd or application config files. Fix: Never pass user input to include/require. Use an allowlist of permitted files: $allowed = ['home', 'about', 'contact']; if (in_array($page, $allowed, true)) { include __DIR__ . '/pages/' . $page . '.php'; } Also set allow_url_include = Off in php.ini.

PHP's loose equality operator (==) performs type coercion before comparing. This enables 'magic hash' exploits where hash strings beginning with '0e' are coerced to 0.0 in scientific notation and compare equal to any other '0e...' hash string. Comparing a numeric-looking user string with == 0 evaluates to true in PHP < 8. CISA identifies weak authentication logic as a preventable root cause of authentication failures.
== $token
Fix: Use strict equality (===) for all security-sensitive comparisons in PHP. For password verification use password_verify(), which performs a constant-time comparison. For HMAC or token comparison use hash_equals($known, $provided).
Category: CISA: Authentication Failures

public/.htaccess 4 warning4 info
🟡 WARNING HDR-MISSING-HSTS public/.htaccess — Line 1 Learn more ↗
Missing Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) header
No Strict-Transport-Security header is configured. Without HSTS, browsers may connect via plain HTTP, exposing users to downgrade and man-in-the-middle attacks.
(header not found in this file)
Fix: Add: Header always set Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload"
Category: HTTP Security Headers
🟡 WARNING HDR-MISSING-CSP public/.htaccess — Line 1 Learn more ↗
Missing Content-Security-Policy header
No Content-Security-Policy header is configured. Without it the browser places no restriction on which resources can be loaded, making XSS and data-injection attacks significantly more impactful.
(header not found in this file)
Fix: Add a Content-Security-Policy header. A safe starting point: Header always set Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'"
Category: HTTP Security Headers
🟡 WARNING HDR-MISSING-XFO public/.htaccess — Line 1 Learn more ↗
Missing X-Frame-Options header
X-Frame-Options is not set. Without it the page can be embedded in a frame or iframe on any origin, enabling clickjacking attacks.
(header not found in this file)
Fix: Add: Header always set X-Frame-Options "DENY" (use SAMEORIGIN if same-site framing is required).
Category: HTTP Security Headers
🟡 WARNING HDR-MISSING-XCTO public/.htaccess — Line 1 Learn more ↗
Missing X-Content-Type-Options header
X-Content-Type-Options is not set. Without 'nosniff', browsers may MIME-sniff responses and execute non-script files as scripts.
(header not found in this file)
Fix: Add: Header always set X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff"
Category: HTTP Security Headers
🔵 INFO HDR-MISSING-REFERRER-POLICY public/.htaccess — Line 1 Learn more ↗
Missing Referrer-Policy header
Referrer-Policy is not set. Without it the browser may include the full URL in the Referer header sent to third-party sites, leaking sensitive path and query-string data.
(header not found in this file)
Fix: Add: Header always set Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
Category: HTTP Security Headers
🔵 INFO HDR-MISSING-PERMISSIONS-POLICY public/.htaccess — Line 1 Learn more ↗
Missing Permissions-Policy header
Permissions-Policy is not set. Without it the browser may grant access to sensitive APIs (camera, microphone, geolocation) to pages or injected scripts without restriction.
(header not found in this file)
Fix: Add: Header always set Permissions-Policy "geolocation=(), camera=(), microphone=()"
Category: HTTP Security Headers
🔵 INFO HDR-MISSING-COOP public/.htaccess — Line 1 Learn more ↗
Missing Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy (COOP) header
Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy is not set. Without it, attackers may gain a reference to your window object via cross-origin pop-ups, enabling cross-origin information leakage (e.g. XS-Leaks) and Spectre-style attacks.
(header not found in this file)
Fix: Add: Header always set Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy "same-origin" (use same-origin-allow-popups if pop-up functionality is required)
Category: HTTP Security Headers
🔵 INFO HDR-MISSING-XSS-PROTECTION public/.htaccess — Line 1 Learn more ↗
Missing X-XSS-Protection header
X-XSS-Protection is not explicitly configured. Modern browsers ignore this header in favour of CSP, but explicitly setting it to 0 prevents older browsers from enabling a built-in XSS filter that can introduce new vulnerabilities.
(header not found in this file)
Fix: Add: Header always set X-XSS-Protection "0" (OWASP recommends disabling the legacy filter; rely on Content-Security-Policy instead)
Category: HTTP Security Headers

vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Support/ServiceProvider.php 5 critical
🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-REMOTE-INCLUDE vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Support/ServiceProvider.php — Line 169 Learn more ↗
PHP remote or user-controlled file inclusion
When allow_url_include = On in php.ini, passing a URL to include() / require() fetches and executes arbitrary remote PHP code. Even with allow_url_include = Off, passing user input to include/require enables Local File Inclusion (LFI) and path traversal to sensitive files such as /etc/passwd or application config files. CISA identifies remote code execution via file inclusion as a critical preventable vulnerability.
require $path
Fix: Never pass user input to include/require. Use an allowlist of permitted files: $allowed = ['home', 'about', 'contact']; if (in_array($page, $allowed, true)) { include __DIR__ . '/pages/' . $page . '.php'; } Also set allow_url_include = Off in php.ini.

PHP remote or user-controlled file inclusion
When allow_url_include = On in php.ini, passing a URL to include() / require() fetches and executes arbitrary remote PHP code. Even with allow_url_include = Off, passing user input to include/require enables Local File Inclusion (LFI) and path traversal to sensitive files such as /etc/passwd or application config files. CISA identifies remote code execution via file inclusion as a critical preventable vulnerability.
require_once $file
Fix: Never pass user input to include/require. Use an allowlist of permitted files: $allowed = ['home', 'about', 'contact']; if (in_array($page, $allowed, true)) { include __DIR__ . '/pages/' . $page . '.php'; } Also set allow_url_include = Off in php.ini.

vendor/phpstan/phpdoc-parser/src/Parser/TokenIterator.php 4 critical
🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-TYPE-JUGGLING vendor/phpstan/phpdoc-parser/src/Parser/TokenIterator.php — Line 136 Learn more ↗
PHP loose equality (==) used with password, hash, or token value
PHP's loose equality operator (==) performs type coercion before comparing. This enables 'magic hash' exploits where hash strings beginning with '0e' are coerced to 0.0 in scientific notation and compare equal to any other '0e...' hash string. Comparing a numeric-looking user string with == 0 evaluates to true in PHP < 8. CISA identifies weak authentication logic as a preventable root cause of authentication failures.
== $tokenType
Fix: Use strict equality (===) for all security-sensitive comparisons in PHP. For password verification use password_verify(), which performs a constant-time comparison. For HMAC or token comparison use hash_equals($known, $provided).
Category: CISA: Authentication Failures

PHP loose equality (==) used with password, hash, or token value
PHP's loose equality operator (==) performs type coercion before comparing. This enables 'magic hash' exploits where hash strings beginning with '0e' are coerced to 0.0 in scientific notation and compare equal to any other '0e...' hash string. PHP loose equality (==) used with password, hash, or token value
PHP's loose equality operator (==) performs type coercion before comparing. This enables 'magic hash' exploits where hash strings beginning with '0e' are coerced to 0.0 in scientific notation and compare equal to any other '0e...' hash string. Comparing a numeric-looking user string with == 0 evaluates to true in PHP < 8. CISA identifies weak authentication logic as a preventable root cause of authentication failures.
== $token
Fix: Use strict equality (===) for all security-sensitive comparisons in PHP. For password verification use password_verify(), which performs a constant-time comparison. For HMAC or token comparison use hash_equals($known, $provided).

PHP unserialize() called with user-controlled data
Passing user-supplied data to PHP's unserialize() allows Object Injection attacks. If the codebase contains gadget chains (magic methods such as __wakeup(), __destruct(), or __toString()), an attacker can trigger arbitrary code execution, file deletion, or other destructive actions. Fix: Never deserialize data from untrusted sources. Use json_decode() for data interchange. If PHP objects must be transferred, use a signed token format (e.g. JWT) and validate the signature before deserializing. Alternatively, use the Symfony Serializer with an explicit type allowlist.

PHP dynamic class instantiation from user-controlled variable

PHP loose equality (==) used with password, hash, or token value
PHP's loose equality operator (==) performs type coercion before comparing. This enables 'magic hash' exploits where hash strings beginning with '0e' are coerced to 0.0 in scientific notation and compare equal to any other '0e...' hash string. Comparing a numeric-looking user string with == 0 evaluates to true in PHP < 8. CISA identifies weak authentication logic as a preventable root cause of authentication failures.
== $lastCodes
Fix: Use strict equality (===) for all security-sensitive comparisons in PHP. For password verification use password_verify(), which performs a constant-time comparison. For HMAC or token comparison use hash_equals($known, $provided).
Category: CISA: Authentication Failures

🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-UNSERIALIZE vendor/ramsey/uuid/src/Provider/Node/NodeProviderCollection.php — Line 43 Learn more ↗
PHP unserialize() called with user-controlled data
Passing user-supplied data to PHP's unserialize() allows Object Injection attacks. If the codebase contains gadget chains (magic methods such as __wakeup(), __destruct(), or __toString()), an attacker can trigger arbitrary code execution, file deletion, or other destructive actions. CISA lists insecure deserialization as a root cause of preventable vulnerabilities.
unserialize($serialized
Fix: Never deserialize data from untrusted sources. Use json_decode() for data interchange. If PHP objects must be transferred, use a signed token format (e.g. JWT) and validate the signature before deserializing. Alternatively, use the Symfony Serializer with an explicit type allowlist.
Category: CISA: Insecure Deserialization

vendor/symfony/routing/Router.php 2 critical
🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-REMOTE-INCLUDE vendor/symfony/routing/Router.php — Line 301 Learn more ↗
PHP remote or user-controlled file inclusion
When allow_url_include = On in php.ini, passing a URL to include() / require() fetches and executes arbitrary remote PHP code. Even with allow_url_include = Off, passing user input to include/require enables Local File Inclusion (LFI) and path traversal to sensitive files such as /etc/passwd or application config files. CISA identifies remote code execution via file inclusion as a critical preventable vulnerability.
require $path
Fix: Never pass user input to include/require. Use an allowlist of permitted files: $allowed = ['home', 'about', 'contact']; if (in_array($page, $allowed, true)) { include __DIR__ . '/pages/' . $page . '.php'; } Also set allow_url_include = Off in php.ini.

preg_match('/\b(if|for|foreach|while|switch|else|elseif|do)\s*\([^)]*\)\s*$/'
Fix: Anchor validation patterns: preg_match('/^[a-z0-9]{1,32}$/i', $input). The ^ asserts start-of-string and $ asserts end-of-string.
Category: Input Validation

vendor/nikic/php-parser/lib/PhpParser/PrettyPrinterAbstract.php 2 critical
🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-TYPE-JUGGLING vendor/nikic/php-parser/lib/PhpParser/PrettyPrinterAbstract.php — Line 708 Learn more ↗
PHP loose equality (==) used with password, hash, or token value
PHP's loose equality operator (==) performs type coercion before comparing. This enables 'magic hash' exploits where hash strings beginning with '0e' are coerced to 0.0 in scientific notation and compare equal to any other '0e...' hash string. Comparing a numeric-looking user string with == 0 evaluates to true in PHP < 8. CISA identifies weak authentication logic as a preventable root cause of authentication failures.
== $findToken
Fix: Use strict equality (===) for all security-sensitive comparisons in PHP. For password verification use password_verify(), which performs a constant-time comparison. For HMAC or token comparison use hash_equals($known, $provided).
Category: CISA: Authentication Failures

🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-UNSERIALIZE vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Bus/DynamoBatchRepository.php — Line 514 Learn more ↗
PHP unserialize() called with user-controlled data
Passing user-supplied data to PHP's unserialize() allows Object Injection attacks. If the codebase contains gadget chains (magic methods such as __wakeup(), __destruct(), or __toString()), an attacker can trigger arbitrary code execution, file deletion, or other destructive actions. CISA lists insecure deserialization as a root cause of preventable vulnerabilities.
unserialize($serialized
Fix: Never deserialize data from untrusted sources. Use json_decode() for data interchange. If PHP objects must be transferred, use a signed token format (e.g. JWT) and validate the signature before deserializing. Alternatively, use the Symfony Serializer with an explicit type allowlist.

PHP loose equality (==) used with password, hash, or token value
PHP's loose equality operator (==) performs type coercion before comparing. This enables 'magic hash' exploits where hash strings beginning with '0e' are coerced to 0.0 in scientific notation and compare equal to any other '0e...' hash string. Comparing a numeric-looking user string with == 0 evaluates to true in PHP < 8. CISA identifies weak authentication logic as a preventable root cause of authentication failures.
== $hash
Fix: Use strict equality (===) for all security-sensitive comparisons in PHP. For password verification use password_verify(), which performs a constant-time comparison. For HMAC or token comparison use hash_equals($known, $provided).

🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-REMOTE-INCLUDE vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Foundation/Bootstrap/LoadConfiguration.php — Line 115 Learn more ↗
PHP remote or user-controlled file inclusion
When allow_url_include = On in php.ini, passing a URL to include() / require() fetches and executes arbitrary remote PHP code. Even with allow_url_include = Off, passing user input to include/require enables Local File Inclusion (LFI) and path traversal to sensitive files such as /etc/passwd or application config files. CISA identifies remote code execution via file inclusion as a critical preventable vulnerability.

Fix: Never pass user input to include/require. Use an allowlist of permitted files: $allowed = ['home', 'about', 'contact']; if (in_array($page, $allowed, true)) { include __DIR__ . '/pages/' . $page . '.php'; } Also set allow_url_include = Off in php.ini.

PHP remote or user-controlled file inclusion

🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-DYNAMIC-CLASS vendor/symfony/uid/Factory/UuidFactory.php — Line 52 Learn more ↗
PHP dynamic class instantiation from user-controlled variable
Instantiating a PHP class from a user-supplied string (new $$userInput(), new $classFromRequest()) allows an attacker to instantiate any autoloaded class. If constructors or magic methods perform file operations, network calls, or code evaluation, this leads to remote code execution. CISA identifies this as insufficient input validation enabling injection.
new $class(
Fix: Never instantiate classes from user-supplied strings. Use an explicit allowlist: $allowed = ['Foo', 'Bar']; if (in_array($className, $allowed, true)) { $obj = new $className(); } A factory function with a match/switch on known class names is the safest pattern.
Category: CISA: Injection

vendor/ramsey/uuid/src/Type/Integer.php 1 critical
🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-UNSERIALIZE vendor/ramsey/uuid/src/Type/Integer.php — Line 116 Learn more ↗
PHP unserialize() called with user-controlled data
Passing user-supplied data to PHP's unserialize() allows Object Injection attacks. If the codebase contains gadget chains (magic methods such as __wakeup(), __destruct(), or __toString()), an attacker can trigger arbitrary code execution, file deletion, or other destructive actions. CISA lists insecure deserialization as a root cause of preventable vulnerabilities.
unserialize($data
Fix: Never deserialize data from untrusted sources. Use json_decode() for data interchange. If PHP objects must be transferred, use a signed token format (e.g. JWT) and validate the signature before deserializing. Alternatively, use the Symfony Serializer with an explicit type allowlist.
Category: CISA: Insecure Deserialization

PHP's loose equality operator (==) performs type coercion before comparing. This enables 'magic hash' exploits where hash strings beginning with '0e' are coerced to 0.0 in scientific notation and compare equal to any other '0e...' hash string. vendor/symfony/console/Messenger/RunCommandMessageHandler.php 1 critical
🔴 CRITICAL CISA-PHP-TYPE-JUGGLING vendor/symfony/console/Messenger/RunCommandMessageHandler.php — Line 50 Learn more ↗
PHP loose equality (==) used with password, hash, or token value
PHP's loose equality operator (==) performs type coercion before comparing. This enables 'magic hash' exploits where hash strings beginning with '0e' are coerced to 0.0 in scientific notation and compare equal to any other '0e...' hash string. Comparing a numeric-looking user string with == 0 evaluates to true in PHP < 8. CISA identifies weak authentication logic as a preventable root cause of authentication failures.
== $exitCode
Fix: Use strict equality (===) for all security-sensitive comparisons in PHP. For password verification use password_verify(), which performs a constant-time comparison. For HMAC or token comparison use hash_equals($known, $provided).
Category: CISA: Authentication Failures

🟡 WARNING PHP-IV-REGEX-NO-ANCHORS vendor/symfony/console/Input/Input.php — Line 156 Learn more ↗
preg_match() pattern missing start/end anchors
A regex used for validation without ^ and $ anchors only checks for a match anywhere in the string. An attacker can prepend or append malicious content that still satisfies the regex. OWASP recommends anchoring all validation patterns.
preg_match('{^[\w-]+$}'
Fix: Anchor validation patterns: preg_match('/^[a-z0-9]{1,32}$/i', $input). The ^ asserts start-of-string and $ asserts end-of-string.
Category: Input Validation
